Absolutely loved this café! I tried their Bravacado toast which came with delicious sweet potato fries, and the Sabbaba wrap with salad and fries on the side — both were super fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. I was so excited to dig in that I actually forgot to take a photo of the wrap! 😄

Definitely going back soon to try their salads and bowls — if they’re anything like what I had today, I’m sure they’ll be amazing!

featured_reviews.name: Dinesh Katke
featured_reviews.review_text:
Just had a fantastic meal at Project Hum. If you think healthy eating means compromising on taste, this place will change your mind.

Chocolate Smoothie: Mind-blown that this is sugar-free! It was rich and perfectly sweet; you’d never guess it was the healthier choice.

Spiced Grilled Chicken Breast: Hand down the best chicken breast I’ve ever had. Super juicy and perfectly cooked. The "Hum green paste" on top is a game changer.

Sides: The sweet potato fries and sprouts salad were fresh and delicious.

Vibe & Service:
The ambience is great and the staff are incredibly polite. A huge plus for the clean and hygienic washrooms. It’s also pet-friendly.
Note: Parking can be a bit tricky, so plan accordingly. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Cocktail King
featured_reviews.review_text:
Found it overrated. Was looking forward to the farm to table concept. We ordered 3 sandwiches - Prawn Ghee Roast, Korean Chicken & Broc n Roll. We also ordered 3 mango milkshakes. Service was non existent. No water served. We ordered our food at the counter which is ok. Sandwiches took 30+ minutes. We asked for menu several times but were given one after we had finished eating. This took away anything else that we would have ordered since we didnt have menus.

Coming to the food. The Sour Dough used for the sandwiches was just too chewy. Our jaws started hurting (no exaggeration) trying to finish them. We were in no mood to complain as we were already late and noone in the restaurant seemed bothered about it anyway. The Korean chicken sandwich tasted off. The flavours didnt go well with the sour dough. Should have been in a milk bun. The fries were excellent! The milk shake again was just ok. Nothing special.

The meal felt very expensive (I know its Bandra) for the over quality of food.

Hope they get better.

featured_reviews.name: Raj doesn't share food
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Veranda around 4 PM, and the first thing to note is that the kitchen was partially closed at that time, which limited a few options. Still, we managed to order a decent variety of dishes.
We tried prawns thecha, chicken 65, chicken tenders, pizza, pasta, and Hakka noodles. Most of the food was actually good and enjoyable. The highlight of the meal was definitely the prawns thecha, easily the best dish on the table. It was flavorful, well-cooked, and something I’d genuinely go back for.
The pizza and pasta were nice, chicken 65 was solid, and overall the food quality was pretty satisfying. But the Hakka noodles were a letdown. They had a strong smell, likely from the egg and chicken, which made it hard to enjoy the dish.
Another downside was the timing of the chicken tenders. They arrived way too late, almost after we were done eating everything else, which kind of ruined the flow of the meal.
That said, the ambience is where Veranda really stands out. The place looks amazing, has a great vibe, and the location is perfect for a chill outing in Bandra.
Overall, it’s a good place with great ambience and mostly good food, but a few issues with timing and consistency in dishes hold it back slightly.

featured_reviews.name: Ramsha Tausalkar
featured_reviews.review_text: There’s a spot in Bandra that serves North Indian food so good, you’ll forget that you’re in Mumbai and be transported straight to Punjab. It’s called Papa Pancho Da Dhaba and they’ve got a menu that’s small and straightforward - but they do these dishes so well and in such an authentic manner - we for sure haven’t had such North Indian food in Mumbai. The Dal Makhani, Cheese Kulcha, Makhani Chicken, Kasturi Kebab, Dahi Papdi Chaat and Matka Kulfi - all of your seemingly regular dishes but here it’s all elevated, rich and very real. The interiors are colourful and very dhaba-like. If this is a cuisine you enjoy, save this spot!

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Kartik Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Papa Pancho da dhaba is a kind of experience amidst the by-lanes of hype Bandra Pali Hill. You get into this colourful world of roadside dhabas as soon as you step in. Sparkly danglers, colourful patakas, slogans written on trucks decorated on the walls.
Food:
Good, guilty and gluttonous North Indian food is served with love on brass cutlery. You feel the butter in every bite. Quality is great, though quantity is frequently insufficient for a couple of people. Earlier they used to include dal makhani and dahi etc. with their mouthwatering kulchas and parathas but now they have stopped doing that. Tandoori Starters and tandoor breads are must try for.
Service: servers are frank and friendly and a bit too nosy sometimes.
Ambience: small place, but they made max out of it. They transfer you to dhaba instantly.
Value for money: This would disappoint you, as for what they ask for; their quantity is too little. Hope they work on their quantity.
A highly recommended place for small group or family to visit if you are craving some good Kulchas, Parathas, Tandooris and a glass full of lassi.

featured_reviews.name: Exploreonmind
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited this beautiful celebrity owned bungalow restaurant and absolutely loved the experience. The space is stunning, with thoughtfully designed interiors, cozy corners, plenty of natural light, and a warm, elegant ambiance that makes you want to stay for hours. Whether you’re planning a leisurely brunch, a special date night, or simply catching up with friends, the atmosphere is perfect.

The food was equally impressive. The Avocado Emerald Sushi was fresh, vibrant, and beautifully presented. The Garci Espanol prawns were packed with flavour and cooked perfectly. The White Butter Chicken paired with fresh breads was rich, comforting, and incredibly satisfying, while the creamy fettuccine pasta was indulgent without feeling heavy. The drinks were refreshing and well crafted, complementing the meal perfectly.

The highlight for me was the Hazelnut Praline Cake rich, decadent, and the perfect ending to a memorable meal.

What truly elevates this place is the overall experience: attentive hospitality, beautiful aesthetics, great food, and an atmosphere that feels both luxurious and welcoming. Easily one of the most picturesque dining spots in the city and definitely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: Harish
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Scarlet House recently and the place immediately stands out for its striking red-themed decor and great location. The ambience feels lively and a bit different from typical restaurants. We were a group of three and managed to get a small private room for about an hour, which made the meal feel relaxed and comfortable.

The food had plenty of character. The prawn curry with Malabar parotta was one of the highlights — the curry was rich and flavorful, and the parotta had those nice layered rings that soak up the gravy well. The caramelised pasta was interesting too, slightly spicy and quite bold in flavour. The white butter chicken was different from the usual version — it felt richer, almost slightly cheese-infused.

We also tried sushi and masala khichdi, both well done. For drinks, the Picante cocktail stood out — spicy, refreshing, and very enjoyable.

They didn’t have the 70% dark chocolate cookie that we wanted to try, so we ended with a gluten-free chocolate cake (around 35% chocolate) instead, which turned out to be a nice way to finish the meal.

Friendly service, interesting decor, and plenty of flavour in the dishes. I’d happily come back to explore more of the menu next time.

featured_reviews.review_text:

We ordered the edamame phyllo mousse and the enoki truffle maki, and absolutely loved both dishes. The edamame phyllo mousse was such an interesting dish and unlike anything I’ve had before, fresh, beautifully done, and full of flavor. Overall, it was a wonderful place to enjoy a meal, with great food and a really welcoming vibe. I would definitely come back again.

customer_updates.name: Yogesh Sharma
customer_updates.text:
South Indian food isn't all idlis and dosas and I'm happy to see a few restaurants such as The Tanjore Tiffin Room that's here to prove this point.

The Jackfruit Cutlet and Sweet Potato Yellow Chilli are great appetizers. I prefer the cutlet more owing to the interesting tangy chutney that's served with it.

We were planning to directly order the main course but our server suggested that we first sample their offerings in the form of a tasting platter. Definitely go for the tasting platter which is provided to you at no cost - it's a beautiful presentation.

It was only after the tasting platter that we opted to go for the Vegetable Madras Railway Curry. The tomato and cream base paired so well with the Malabar Parotta.

Our server recommended the Lemongrass Cooler and it was a refreshing choice.

featured_reviews.name: Aniket
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Tanjore Tiffin Room is one of the finest places in the city to enjoy authentic South Indian cuisine in a refined yet welcoming setting. From the moment you enter, the ambience sets the tone — warm, classy, and thoughtfully designed with a blend of traditional and contemporary elements. It strikes the perfect balance between being vibrant and cosy, making it ideal for both family meals and relaxed dining with friends.

The food is truly the star here. Every dish is crafted with rich, traditional flavours that reflect the culinary heritage of South India. The tasting platter is a must-try, offering a wonderful selection of signature items that allow you to sample a variety of dishes in one go. Whether it’s the dosas, curries, or starters, everything is cooked to perfection and beautifully presented. The flavours are authentic without being overly spicy, appealing to a wide range of palates.

The service is excellent, with staff who are attentive, polite, and well-informed about the menu. Their recommendations are spot-on, and they ensure you’re comfortable throughout your visit. Another convenience is the availability of valet parking, which makes dining here hassle-free, especially during busy hours.

Overall, The Tanjore Tiffin Room delivers a delightful South Indian dining experience with great food, superb service, and charming ambience. Highly recommended.

Had lunch at The Village Shop today with my husband and overall it was a good experience. The food was fresh, wholesome, and it’s definitely a great place for people with allergies, dietary restrictions, or specific food preferences.

There was one mix-up where potato was added instead of sweet potato mash in one of the dishes, but the team replaced it with exotic vegetables without any issue, which we appreciated.

Our waiter didn’t seem very well informed about the ingredients and communication could have been better, especially for a place that caters to special diets and allergies. featured_reviews.name: Neeraja Sundar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very ghastly and amusing experience at the Village Shop. I spent a Monday morning here, was hoping to get my coffee and breakfast  in some peace and quiet. It was only me in the cafe and the owner with 2 of her staff on another table.
In the first 10 mins I figured the owner had issues with staff, even though they spoke in hushed tones.

I let it slide. Naturally, I have no context of that conversation.
The food wasn’t up to the mark. They had it replaced without getting defensive.

Then, after a few mins I spoke loudly because I was on a call, and there was no one else in the cafe but me and the owner, I was asked to speak softly. She was irked. I gladly obliged.

I stepped outside to take my call. For 45 mins. In the heat. You see, I have been brought up with a lot of empathy.
It felt like my grandmother gave me a punishment to not enter the house.

What a ghastly experience for a Bandra cafe.  I hope the owners have the business acumen to start something else of their own. Customer centricity and empathy are not the strongest suit of some of the most affluent people in Bandra. What tarnishes reputation is lack of empathy for staff and no understanding of what customer focus looks like.

Money can’t buy you manners or class.

Its evident to me today, yet again :)

featured_reviews.name: Noor Sayeed Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries in Bandra has such a gorgeous, welcoming vibe, it’s easily one of the prettiest spots for South Indian food in the city. The staff was genuinely sweet and the service was so smooth it made the whole experience feel really relaxed.

We decided to try their new chaat menu, and the Shakkarkand Matar ki Chaat was a total winner, it felt super fresh and not at all oily. The Chatpata Singhada (water chestnut) was a fun surprise too, especially for that unique crunch you don't usually find in street food.

The Madras Diaries Special Combo is a solid choice if you’re like me and can't decide the medu vada was perfectly crispy. But honestly, the real highlight was the Filter Coffee with those Rawa Biscuits. It’s such a nostalgic, comforting pairing. We finished with the Elaneer Payasum, which was light and refreshing, though I wish there was just a bit more of it! Definitely worth a visit if you’re in Bandra and want a meal that feels both clean and satisfying.

featured_reviews.name: Allen Samuel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries is a perfect blend of authentic South Indian comfort and exciting new flavours! The highlight now is their chaat menu, which adds a fun, chatpata twist alongside their classic offerings.

The Chatpata Singhada and Shakkarkand Matar Ki Chaat were vibrant, tangy, and full of flavour. The Chettinad Paneer with flaky wheat parotta was rich and satisfying, paired beautifully with the soft Kodumai (wheat) parotta. Refreshing sips like the Cold Coffee and Virgin Mojito balanced the meal, while the Elaneer Payasam was a light, delicious finish.

The presentation of each dish was impressive and clearly made with attention to detail. Service was warm and prompt, making the overall experience even more enjoyable.

With its warm décor and relaxed, inviting ambience, Madras Diaries is a must-visit for a wholesome meal with a unique chaat twist!

featured_reviews.name: Aaniket R Naddkarni
featured_reviews.review_text:
VARUGA VARUGA ❤️

Everyone is craving South Indian food these days… looks like Idli & Dosa have officially become Gen Z’s favorite comfort food 😍
So we decided to check out Madras Diaries in Bandra — a place already famous for authentic South Indian food, but now they’ve also launched CHATS… and trust me, this will make you visit again & again!

Without wasting any time, we started with our favorite — Pani Puri 🤤
And bhai sahab… they served it with 3 different flavor waters — Mumbai style, Delhiwala & Kolkata style!
We literally couldn’t stop eating 😅

Then came the Palak Patta Chaat…
And bhai, ekdum Delhi ki yaad dila di ❤️

To beat the summer heat, we tried their Kokum Cooler & Mint Cooler — super refreshing and fresh!

For mains, we ordered Mini Idlies served with 4 different chutneys… and trust me, this combo is something you’ll only get here, so make sure it’s on your order list ✔️

We also tried the Malabar Paratha with Chettinad Paneer — great quantity, rich flavors, and the paneer was super soft 😍

And finally in desserts, Pineapple Sheera… simple, comforting, and honestly made with love ❤️
So make sure you visit Madras Diaries

featured_reviews.name: Omkar More
featured_reviews.review_text:
I hae been a regular at EAC since 2019. It has been my go-to for years, and while it remains a staple in my Bandra circuit, have noticed some shifts lately that are hard to ignore.
The freshness of their ingredients is honestly amazing - you can taste the quality in every bite. Over the years, I have tried almost everything on the menu across all sections, except for their new bread menu and the salads.
​The Food Journey
​When it comes to the food, I have had nearly all their desserts. If they have the Opera Pastry, it is a absolute must-try. On the other hand, the Tiramisu was just average. If you're going for a drink, the Pineapple Coriander Cooler and the Spiced Mojito are my absolute favorites, but the Vietnamese Cold Coffee is extremely bad - a hard skip.
For mains, their Chicken Burgers, especially the Peri Peri and Grilled Chicken, are top-notch. The Paneer Roasted Veggie Sandwich is also amazing. If you are there for breakfast, the Eggs Benedict is definitely the highlight.
​Pro Tip: You have to try their Roast Chicken with Mashed Potatoes; it is easily their most famous and iconic dish. Hard skip - anything fish.
However, lately, I have noticed the quality seems to have taken a dip. It is not a massive drop, but they have been increasing their SKUs (adding more items), and it is hard not to notice that the consistency isn't what it used to be.
The seating layout here is easily the best of any cafe in Bandra, but a recent experience with the crowd has made me think about stopping my visits completely.
​We were sitting near a table that was loud - uncomfortably loud. A man accompanied by two ladies spent hours shouting. It started with "India vs. Pakistan" and how "we will decimate them," then moved to "India vs. USA" and how the USA is so much better. It turned ugly when he started shitting on Hinduism, calling it a "pagan religion" and preaching Christianity. He kept saying India is "poor, filthy, and bad" because of Hindus and that people should go to churches to "get civilized."
It was highly uncomfortable and left us feeling genuinely shook. I took three weeks to think about whether I should even post this, but the experience was that bad.

Time to hunt for a new go to place.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I’m a regular at Kitchen Garden, Bandra, and wanted to share a consistent issue I’ve experienced over a few visits.

The café is listed as opening at 7:30 AM, and I’ve stopped by a few times around then after morning workouts. However, each time, the team has still been in the middle of setting up—cleaning, switching on machines—and not ready to serve even a simple coffee. If 7:30 AM is the stated opening time, it would be reasonable to expect at least basic service from then. Otherwise, it may be more accurate to list the opening time as 8:00 AM.

More importantly, on a couple of occasions, the person managing the morning shift (appears to be a lady dressed in black in a supervisory role) has responded in a rather abrupt and not very welcoming manner—almost as if customers are interrupting the opening process. It came across as dismissive, and at times borderline rude. This is what prompted me to finally write this.

I enjoy the space and have otherwise had good experiences here, which is why I hope this feedback is taken constructively. A more prepared and welcoming start to the day would make a big difference, especially given the number of early-morning visitors in the neighbourhood.

We had a great dining experience at Naploi in Carter Road, Bandra. From the cozy, welcoming ambiance to the prompt and friendly service, everything was spot on.

Our Server ZUI was very friendly and suggested us their best dishes. She also suggested us what is good in vegetarian dishes and we were glad that we got the best vegetarian option suggested by ZUI! 😊👍

We tried a delicious spread — succulent chicken skewer, rich chicken lasagna, and perfectly cooked spaghetti. The chicken skewers were flavorful and tender, grilled to perfection. Each dish brought a taste of authentic Italian cuisine, and we were impressed with both the quality and portion size.

Desserts were the perfect finale — their famous tiramisu was luxuriously creamy and balanced, while the Spanish churros were crispy on the outside, soft inside, and served with a chocolate ice cream and dark chocolate powder that made them irresistible.

If you’re a fan of Italian food or just looking for a cozy place to enjoy a flavorful meal, Napoli by Shatranj is a must-visit. Can’t wait to return and try more from their menu. 🍷🇮🇹

Their wine selection is impressive, catering to various tastes, and vegetarians will appreciate the many thoughtful options on the menu. Highly recommend for a memorable dining experience!

featured_reviews.name: Komal Nagrani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Paash Bandra: A Quaint Hidden Gem with World-Class Service
Paash in Bandra is a beautiful, quiet little hidden cafe that’s perfect if you want to escape the usual city rush.

Pros:

* Mind-blowing Hospitality: The service here is honestly on another level. The staff noticed I wasn't really vibing with the coffee I ordered and—without me saying a single word or complaining—they proactively brought me a different coffee on the house. Their ability to read a guest's reaction and prioritize your experience is so rare.

* Delicious Food: Service from the kitchen was super quick, and the food was genuinely delicious with really authentic flavors.

* Great Ambiance (9/10): It has a lovely, cozy environment that’s perfect to just sit back, read, or get some thoughts down. They also have a beautiful in-house Khadi boutique store inside which adds a nice touch.

Cons & Improvisation Points:

* Limited Menu: The food options are a bit limited right now; adding a few more dishes would definitely elevate the place.

* A Bit Rushed: While the fast service is great, the vibe feels slightly geared toward a quick turnaround. I wish they’d encourage more of a "work-from-cafe" culture where you can just blend into the environment and linger longer without feeling the need to rush out.

Overall: Highly recommended. The incredible staff alone makes it worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: Avril Dsouza
featured_reviews.review_text: Paashh is located in a quaint lane off Pali Hill, Bandra, and is set in a beautiful and charming heritage Portuguese bungalow. Love the look, vibe and ambience. We had the gazpachio, chaat, paneer tikka, jackfruit nihari, so much more. Did you know the head chef is MasterChef Chef Ajay Chopra, had the opportunity to meet him and discuss food with him. Loved every second.

featured_reviews.name: Yash Rungta
featured_reviews.review_text:
A recent vegan lunch at Rare Earth Cafe turned out to be a genuinely delightful surprise.

Coming from a vegetarian family but someone who enjoys meat and seafood outside, I’ve always felt that the real advantage of being non-vegetarian is the freedom to eat anything—vegan, Jain, or otherwise. This place reinforces that idea beautifully.

Their cashew cheese is truly top-notch. It’s different from dairy cheese, but in a way that feels like an upgrade rather than a compromise. Everything tastes thoughtfully crafted. The flours they use—millets or emmer wheat—are light and easy to digest, which you can actually feel after the meal.

And the dessert? Easily a 7-star experience.

What stands out is their commitment to making everything in-house, using natural ingredients as much as possible. It shows in every bite.

You don’t need to be vegan to enjoy this place. Whether you’re vegetarian, non-vegetarian, eggetarian, Jain, or vegan—this café is absolutely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Locomo Express Hostel recommended Khoa Piyo Restaurant, and I visited there alone for dinner.

I asked for Kingfisher Ultra, and the manager initially confirmed that it was available. However, after a few minutes, another staff member came and informed me that it was not available and that only other brands were in stock. I then requested Budweiser, which was served.

The beer was served without any complimentary snacks like nuts or chips. I also had to ask separately for drinking water, whereas normally water is brought to the table automatically for customers.

I ordered chicken biryani, which was just okay.

After finishing my meal, I requested the bill, and the brought the QR code for payment. However, the manager took the bill from my hand with visible irritation, which felt uncomfortable and unprofessional.

When I was leaving, no staff member was present at the door to open it or even acknowledge me. Two staff members were sitting near the entrance, talking to each other, but there was no courtesy, greeting, or farewell shown.

Overall, I felt the service lacked basic hospitality, professionalism, and customer respect. I hope the management will take this feedback positively and improve their service standards.

featured_reviews.name: Danish Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Toooo Goooddd!!! This place offers so many cuisines that your mind will be confused right from the start. It includes everything from indian and sindhi to mexican, italian and arabic; also offers asian and exotic food items such as fondues. Has a seating area on entry and on the first floor too. Coming to my experience here, it was a mixed review since we had problems related to the air-conditioner and it's management. We sat on the first floor and there's a staircase to reach there. Ambience at both the levels is great and superb!! While the ambience was great, the air-conditioner was equally unrewarding since they weren't working properly. We even reported that to the staff but they said that they already know it's not working and started pretending that they've called the technicians at 4 in the evening the same day!! So even after coming through such scorching heat outside, the inside wasn't much different. Finally after shifting places thrice, we found a spot where cool air could be felt! Apart from all this the food was sooo yummy, fresh and adequate in quantity that my brain didn't have any other issue to focus on!🙌
Food review-
1.Cream of Tomato with Basil soup- 5/5 for quantity, 5/5 for taste. Also they serve extra croutons if asked for!!🤭
2. Pahadi paneer tikka- 5/5 for quantity, 5/5 for taste. The paneer pieces were soooo soft and felt really fresh!!
3. Lasagne Ala Napolitano- 3/5 for quantity, 4/5 for taste. Was less in quantity as compared to other places i've had lasagne. Less cheesy as per the standard flavour of lasagne.
4. Dum aloo punjabi- 10/5 for quantity, 10/5 for taste. Reallly reallly very goood in everythinggg from quantity to taste to the dum aloo pieces. Usually 1 potato is provided but here 2 were provided and it's masala and gravy was also soo yummm!!!😋
5. Butter kulcha- 5/5 for taste. Soft, fresshhhh and buttery!!
6. Chinese sizzler- 1/5 for quantity and 1/5 for taste. Typically a chinese sizzler consists of rice, noodles, manchurian balls, chinese gravy and sautéd veggies. But this consisted just of rice, noodles and sautéd veggies. There were no manchurian balls nor there was any gravy which adds to the taste in sizzlers. REALLY A BIG WASTE OF MONEY, I WOULDN'T RECOMMEND YOU TO ORDER ANY SIZZLER AFTER TRYING THIS ONE AS THIS WAS OVERPRICED AS COMPARED TO ANY OTHER PLACE.
7. Basil Citrus Breeze Margarita- 5/5 for look, 3/5 for taste. Looks too fancy and delicious but is just okay. Full of ice and  essence. Won't matter if you don't try this.

featured_reviews.name: Prakash P
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a good experience trying their sigature favourites. The Pav Bhaji was flavorful, and the Idli was light and fresh. We paired them with their juices, which were clearly made to order.

​Vibe: Basic and functional. They have separate AC and Non-AC sections depending on your preference.

​Service: Excellent. The staff is quick on their feet and very observant.

​Overall, a reliable place for quality food without the fuss.

featured_reviews.name: flp kolkata best hitts
featured_reviews.review_text: The food is delicious, they serve food like family, which is a good practice and the quality of the food is also very good. I am really happy to find South Indian recipes at Shabari Pure Vegetarian Restaurant.

featured_reviews.name: Gaurav Hegde
featured_reviews.review_text:
The food is good but the ambience and cleanliness could be better.
We sat in the ac section and it had some mosquitoes and flies roaming around which was annoying.
The service was quick and the food was delicious.
We got the cheese pav bhaji, Mumbai sandwich, rava masala dosa, and tomato omelette along with coffee and fresh lime soda.

A good spot next to the station if u want some good food in the area

featured_reviews.name: Mohamed Lokhandwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Shabari Restaurant near Santacruz Railway for the second time in two weeks to have a quick lunch.
Fortunately,  this time the food was good and not disappointing like the Pav Bhaji last week which was not upto the mark.
This time we had Paneer Makhanwala with Tandoori Roti and luckily it turned out to be delicious choice  and the portion was also decent enough for two people to eat well.
For Dessert we had Chickoo milkshake and that also was excellent and not disappointing like the mango milk shake last time.
Hope they maintain consistency so that we can visit often.
Mohamed Lokhandwala

featured_reviews.name: Neerja Tiwari
featured_reviews.review_text:
An excellent midrange restaurant
Visited Shabari for a quick lunch
It’s right near the Santacruz Station and so easily accessible to the office going crowd
It’s nearly always full but the turnaround is also v fast
There is seating in two levels for those wanting aircond
to sit in an  Ac section and a non AC section as well
Ambience is average and pretty basic say 1/5
Cutlery is basic and should be improved on 1/5
Service is efficient and courteous 4/5
Specially wish to commend Guddu Shah who took good care of us
Food: 4/5
Ordered
Pav Bhaji : no other word than excellent
Rawa Onion Masala Dosa: The dosa was crisp but the potatoes very okayish
The sambhar was watery and after the first taste : left it
The chutney was mediocre so wont be recommending their South Indian fare
Schezwan Rice : nice and light and just right
Kulfi Falooda: we ordered two to share amongst six and were very happy with the dessert
Recommend this as well
Rating it a Four because of the food and the service
The cost came to about 180 Rs per person
